item.title: Gas prices surge across the region as the war in the Middle East continues - European Western Balkans
item.description: The current conflict in the Middle East, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, have triggered significant global oil market volatility this week, with Brent crude surging above 100-119 USD per barrel. In spite of the fact that on 20 March oil prices declined by 0.4%, reaching approximately 108 USD a barrel, experts state that the economic consequences cannot be mitigated in the short time.

item.title: Talk of KFOR Drawdown Reveals a Changing US Approach to the Balkans - European Western Balkans
item.description: Lawmakers in Washington are raising concerns over reports that the Trump administration is considering scaling back US forces in Kosovo.

item.title: Truck drivers block border crossings across BiH
item.description: SARAJEVO - The Logistics Consortium of Bosnia and Herzegovina has notified the relevant institutions that a protest by transport operators will be held today over restrictions on the length of stay for professional drivers from BiH in Schengen Area countries, which they say effectively denies them the right to work, N1 BiH reports.

item.title: Applications for Kosovo documents using Serbian papers begi
item.description: PRISTINA - Citizens of Kosovo who do not possess Kosovo-issued documents can, starting today, submit applications using Serbia-issued documentation. Applications are being processed through local self-government offices and civil registry services.

item.title: Refocus on fundamental reforms key to Montenegro's EU readiness
item.description: BRUSSELS - During the visit to Belgium, President of Montenegro Jakov Milatović met with European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos. After a meeting, Milatović stated that electoral reform and functionality of the Constitutional Court were among the key topics discussed.

item.title: Slovenia’s Liberal Party Edges Past Right-Wing in Tightly Contested Election - European Western Balkans
item.description: Slovenia’s parliamentary elections concluded with a narrow victory for incumbent Robert Golob and his liberal Freedom Movement party, in a race that highlighted deep political divisions in the EU member state.

item.title: Jeton Zulfaj appointed as Kosovo's Chief Negotiator with the EU
item.description: PRISTINA - Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti has appointed Jeton Zulfaj as Kosovo's chief negotiation with the European Union. As it was stated from Kurti's office, Zulfaj will coordinate Kosovo's EU integration process, with the support of relevant stated institutions.
